To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HepG2 cell expressing human augmenter liver regeneration (hAHR) was successfully established and showed liver specific function when cultured inside the laboratory scale bioreactor.
HepG2 cells stably expressing human ALR were established and that these cells showed liver specific function when cultured in a BAL bioreactor.

the human liver cell line HepG2 hARL was established and showed liver specific functionality in BAL bioreactors, and therefore has the potential to be used as a cell source for the future development of the BAL device.

the establishment of a human cell line that stables expresses ALR and the evaluation of its potential use in BAL.
the use of a human liver cell line that expresses hALR to establish a laboratory scale BAL device.
the establishment of a stable cell line that expresses hALR protein.

the HepG2 ALR stable cell line is a potential candidate for the bioartifical liver in the future.
the cell line that stables expresses human ALR is a potential cell source to be used for the BAL in the future.
this study is the first step toward establishing a cell source for the future BAL device.
